$comment: KC&C design tokens: the single source. Numbers here are parameters; scripts/lib/tokens.ts computes the scales and colours from them (docs/math.md, docs/colour.md). Edit this file, then run `npm run tokens`.

palette.$comment: Ramps in OKLCH. Each step has a fixed lightness L. Chroma c(L) = c_max x (0.35 + 0.65 x sin(pi x L)), so the ends are greyer, then reduced until the colour fits sRGB. Hue is fixed per ramp. A ramp marked flat keeps c_max at every step. The neutral ramp uses the paper's hue (about 90), so greys are warm.

neutral.use: Warm greys: rules, hairlines, control borders, dark surfaces.

green.use: The heavy dark green: better, up, sequential scale.

red.use: The heavy dark red: worse, down, errors.

color.$comment: Semantic colours. A value is a brand anchor (#hex, kept exactly), a ramp step ("green.800") or an explicit oklch(L C H).

paper.use: Page background. KC&C paper; dark is warm umber, not black.

paper-2.use: Sunk area: the reader's own step in a flow strip, code, a selected row.

ink.use: Text, figures, primary button, focus ring.

muted.use: Secondary text: eyebrows, labels, notes, table headers.

rule.use: The 1px rule between sections, above tables, around the flow strip and the legal box.

hair.use: Hairlines between rows and cells. Decorative only.

control.use: Border of inputs, selects, segmented control (3:1).

up.use: Better for the reader. Always with a sign or a word.

down.use: Worse for the reader; errors. Always with a sign or a word.

watch.use: Needs attention, not yet wrong: watch, margin call, sample data.

chart.$comment: Chart marks. Semantic first, then the categorical order, the sequential and the diverging scales.

up.use: Marks that are better for the reader.

down.use: Marks that are worse for the reader.

neutral.use: The baseline series (today, before, earlier periods).

categorical.$comment: Eight series, in this order. Chosen by search (docs/colour.md): every pair keeps an OKLab distance of at least 7 under protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia simulation, and every colour has 3:1 on its paper. Use 1-4 freely; 5-8 only with direct labels.

sequential.$comment: One hue, lightness only, so it reads the same in every colour vision. Low values sit near the paper.

diverging.$comment: Worse (red) to better (green) through a paper-coloured middle. Mirrored steps have the same lightness, so for protanopes the two sides look alike: the side must also be shown by position or a printed sign.

serif.use: Titles, headings, lede, reading text, the big figures.

sans.use: Data and interface: tables, charts, eyebrows, labels, notes, controls, the legal box. Static system fonts only: system-ui is variable on macOS (SF Pro) and its PDF text splits words (docs/evidence.md).

type.$comment: Two scales from one anchor (13 px). Text sizes step by 2 px, because phi is too steep for text you read at length. Display sizes are 13 x sqrt(phi)^k: the KC&C golden scale (13, 21, 34, 55, 89 at even k) with half steps (27, 43 at odd k). docs/math.md explains.

use.xs: Eyebrows, table headers, chart text, footnotes, pills.
use.sm: Data: tables, notes, labels, controls, nav.
use.read: Reading text in documents (EB Garamond has a small x-height).
use.2xl: Page title on phones and in apps; compact figures.
use.5xl: One hero number, at most once per page.

bold.use: Sans emphasis: table headers, diff chips, labels, buttons.

head.use: Uppercase table headers and h3 labels.

space.$comment: Fibonacci: s1 = 5, s2 = 8, s(n) = s(n-1) + s(n-2). Consecutive steps approach phi.

use.s1: Label to value; inside a pill.
use.s2: Inside a block: cell padding, list gaps.
use.s3: Section rule to its heading; figure padding.
use.s4: Between blocks inside a section; grid gutter; page gutter on phones.
use.s5: Masthead to title; gap between columns; page gutter on wide screens.

layout.$comment: page = Fibonacci F(16). golden = page / phi and aside = page - golden: the golden split for a main column and a side column. The 12-column grid uses the s4 gutter; the build checks the column width is a whole pixel. measure = readColumns of the grid, chosen so that reading text has about 66 characters a line (measured, docs/math.md); measure-wide = wideColumns, about 75 characters of sans.

none.use: Default: sections, tables, flow strip, legal box, buttons.

small.use: Inputs, selects, pills. Never a card.

fast.use: Colour and underline changes on hover.

evidence.$comment: Floors with a basis in docs/evidence.md. The build checks the tokens against them (scripts/build-tokens.ts) and the page gate checks the rendered pages (scripts/check-pages.ts). Do not change a value without changing its row in docs/evidence.md.

runningTextPx.use: Running text is at least this size. Rello, Pielot and Marcos (CHI 2016): comprehension was worse at 10 and 12 pt (the authors' 12 pt is about 16 px on their display) than at 18 pt. A floor, not an optimum.

lineHeight.use: Running text line height is at least this multiple of the size. Rello et al. 2016: 0.8 x the browser default (about 1.2) lowered comprehension; 1.0 to 1.8 x made no difference to fixations.

minCharsPerLine.use: Running text has more than 25 characters a line. Dyson and Kipping 1998: 25 cpl was read slower than 100 cpl on screen.

targetPx.use: Pointer targets are at least 24 x 24 CSS px, or meet an exception: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (AA).

chartValueAxisPx.use: A chart read for values has a value axis of at least 80 CSS px. Heer and Bostock 2010, experiment 3: 40 px gave more error; no gain above 80 px.

gridGapPx.use: Gridlines are at least 8 CSS px apart. Heer and Bostock 2010: the authors' suggestion from their gridline conditions (not a tested threshold).

minDeltaE.use: Pairs that carry meaning keep an OKLab distance x 100 of at least this under protanopia and deuteranopia simulation (Machado 2009, severity 1). The value is the JND that CSS Color 4 uses in its gamut-mapping algorithm; no study validates it as a colour-vision threshold, so it is a convention. The redundancy rule is the real safeguard.

budget.$comment: Complexity budget per page, checked by the page gate (scripts/check-pages.ts) on the rendered page at 1280 and 320 px. Basis: the owner's reference, Apple HIG Design principles, Simplicity ('removes the unnecessary, with every element earning its place'); the numbers are a convention (docs/evidence.md). value: more fails; warn: this many or more is a warning. Specimens ([data-kc-specimen]) are not counted.

fontSizes.use: Distinct font sizes on a page. A page has at most seven type roles: secondary text (13), data (15), body (17 or 19), lede (21), section heading (27), figure (34 or 43), title (55). More than seven means two sizes play one role.

accentColours.use: Distinct non-neutral colours (OKLab chroma >= 0.04) on a page: the three state colours (up, down, watch) plus at most three series colours. A heatmap ramp counts as one colour, because it encodes one variable.

boxDepth.use: Bordered boxes (a border on all four sides; controls, pills, sheets and slides excepted) do not nest: a box inside a box fails.

borderAndBackground.use: No element other than a control has both a border and a background colour: that is a card. Rules, not cards (DESIGN.md).

headingWords.use: Words in the longest heading. The heading is the finding, in as few words as it takes (Apple HIG Simplicity, 'Be concise'); 11 or 12 words warns, more fails.

contrast.$comment: Pairs measured in both themes. WCAG 2.2 is the gate (min: 4.5 text, 3 graphics); the build fails under it. APCA Lc is recorded against a target (75 body text, 60 data and labels, 45 large or bold UI, 30 graphics) and flagged, not gated. Every categorical, sequential end and diverging end colour is also checked against paper automatically.

pairs.use: Diff chip and pill, worse; errors
